summary: Reidsville-area fire tower, possibly built in the late 1930s and part of a county network for about 80 years; a newspaper reports it was taken down and moved again.

facts.status_note: Taken down in its latest move to Old River Road; no source found says it has been put back up.

evidence.supports: Possibly built in the late 1930s on the western outskirts of Reidsville
evidence.quote: which may have been constructed in the late 1930s on the western outskirts of Reidsville

notes_for_editor: Main source is one Journal article. The cached copy holds only the opening paragraphs (about 945 characters), so the article's date, its earlier-site detail and any staffing are not verified. Two web searches returned summary text with more detail (an earlier site on Highway 147, a mid-1950s move to a Forestry Commission site on Highway 57, two named staff members), but none of it appeared in a page we could read, so none is in the story. The record point 32.07700, -82.09198 lies east of the list's 'reidsville' row (GA376, 32.08314, -82.11401, 205 ft). The Journal places the original tower on Reidsville's western outskirts, nearer the 'reidsville' row, so the two rows may describe the same tower at different dates; not confirmed. The record location is out of date because the tower has been moved, and the Old River Road coordinates are unknown, so no location correction is proposed. The article gives no year for the moves or the build, so no events are entered. The Digital Library of Georgia photos checked (dlg_vang_tat078, Reidsville High School) do not show the tower and were not used.
